Rashi on Pesachim 80b:13:1.hebrew: בקרבנותיהן - דנזיר ועושה פסח. הותרה לו אם נטמא גופו בספק טומאה, וקרבן יחיד אינו דוחה שבת וטומאה:
Rashi on Pesachim 80b:13:1.english: In their offerings - [That is,] of a nazirite and one who offers the Paschal lamb. It was permitted for him if his body became impure with a doubtful impurity, whereas an individual's offering does not override Shabbat and impurity.

Rashi on Pesachim 80b:13:2.hebrew: כי גמירי - דטומאת התהום מותרת להם, בבעלים הוא דגמירי, אבל בכהן לא:
Rashi on Pesachim 80b:13:2.english: When they learned [the oral tradition] - that impurity of the deep is permitted for them, it was with regard to the owners that they learned [it], but not with regard to the priest.

Rashi on Pesachim 80b:13:3.hebrew: או דילמא בזיבחא גמירי - בקרבנות הללו — בפסח ובקרבנות נזיר — גמירי דהותרה להם טומאת התהום של גוף. הילכך, לא שנא בבעלים ולא שנא בכהן:
Rashi on Pesachim 80b:13:3.english: Or perhaps they learned [it] with regard to the sacrifice - [That is,] with regard to these offerings — the Paschal lamb and the offerings of a nazirite — they learned [through oral tradition] that bodily impurity of the deep is permitted for them; therefore, [there is] no difference whether [it is] the owners or the priest.

Rashi on Pesachim 80b:14:1.english: They did not state [the rule of] impurity of the deep - That it was permitted for a nazirite and one who offers the Paschal sacrifice.

Rashi on Pesachim 80b:14:2.english: Only regarding a corpse - But other uncertain impurities were not permitted.

Rashi on Pesachim 80b:15:1.english: And with whom - In whom could this impurity of the depths of a creeping animal occur, [concerning] which it states it was not permitted?

Rashi on Pesachim 80b:15:2.english: If [it applies] to a nazirite, is it effective for him - Even definite impurities of a creeping animal, to void his count and [require] the bringing of his offerings.

Rashi on Pesachim 80b:15:3.hebrew: וכי ימות עליו כתיב - פתע זה שוגג, פתאום זה מזיד, בכריתות (דף ט.):
Rashi on Pesachim 80b:15:3.english: And if [a man] shall die beside him is written - [The verse continues:] "suddenly" [peta] — this refers to an unwitting [act]; "unexpectedly" [pit'om] — this refers to an intentional [act], [as taught] in Keritot (9a).

Rashi on Pesachim 80b:16:1.hebrew: הניחא למאן דאמר - לקמן בפרק האשה (פסחים דף צ:): ה"ג, אלא לאו בכהן:
Rashi on Pesachim 80b:16:1.english: It works out well according to the one who said - [This dispute is] later in the chapter [entitled] HaIshah (Pesachim 90b): This is the reading: "Rather, is [it] not [referring] to a priest?"

Rashi on Pesachim 80b:18:1.hebrew: לעולם בבעלים - ובעושה פסח. ודקשיא לך: הא לא מהניא ביה טומאה אחריתי? איכא טומאת זיבה, שהיא שבעת ימים, ואין שוחטים וזורקים עליו. ואשמעינן רבי חייא דטומאת התהום דזיבה — כגון זב בשביעי שלו, דספק הוא שמא יראה היום ויסתור כל מה שמנה, ספק לא יראה והרי הוא כטמא שרץ דחזי לאורתא — והויא לה טומאת התהום, ופסלא ביה:
Rashi on Pesachim 80b:18:1.english: Actually, [it is] with the owners - and with one who is offering the Paschal lamb. And as for what you asked: "Does no other impurity affect him?" There is the impurity of zivah, which is seven days, and one does not slaughter and sprinkle [the blood] on his behalf. And Rabbi Ḥiyya teaches us that impurity of the deep of zivah — for example, a zav on his seventh [clean] day, where it is uncertain: perhaps he will see [a discharge] today and forfeit all that he counted, [or] perhaps he will not see [a discharge], and behold, he is like one impure from a creeping creature who is fit in the evening — and it is [considered] impurity of the deep, and it disqualifies him.

Rashi on Pesachim 80b:1:1.hebrew: טהרה מדחיא - טומאה לשני, כי עבדי ציבור בטהרה:
Rashi on Pesachim 80b:1:1.english: Purity defers - [those with] impurity to the Second [Pesach], when the community performs [the offering] in purity.

Rashi on Pesachim 80b:3:1.hebrew: בראשון לא עבדי - דהא טמאי מתים מיעוטא. ובשני לא עבדי, דהואיל וטהרו זבין עכשיו, נמצאו רוב ציבור צריכין לו, ורובא דציבור בשני לא עבדי:
Rashi on Pesachim 80b:3:1.english: On the first [Pesach], they do not perform [it] - For those impure with corpse impurity are a minority. And on the second [Pesach], they do not perform [it], for since the zavim have now become pure, the majority of the congregation are found to need it, and a majority of the congregation do not perform [it] on the second [Pesach].

Rashi on Pesachim 80b:4:1.hebrew: הפסח שנזרק את דמו ואח"כ נודע שהוא טמא - הפסח או הדם:
Rashi on Pesachim 80b:4:1.english: The Paschal lamb whose blood was sprinkled, and afterward it became known that it was ritually impure - [Either] the Paschal lamb or the blood.

Rashi on Pesachim 80b:4:2.english: The frontplate appeases - and he is exempt from the second Pesach.

Rashi on Pesachim 80b:4:3.english: They became impure - [meaning] its owners [contracted] impurity of the body from a corpse.

Rashi on Pesachim 80b:4:4.hebrew: אין הציץ מרצה - וחייב לעשות פסח שני, דהא בשעת זריקה לאו בר מיעבד פסח הוא, דרחמנא דחייה:
Rashi on Pesachim 80b:4:4.english: The frontplate does not appease - And he is obligated to observe the second Pesach, for at the time of sprinkling [the blood] he was not fit to perform the Paschal offering, as the Merciful One deferred him.

Rashi on Pesachim 80b:4:5.hebrew: הנזיר - דכתיב ביה (במדבר ו) "וכי ימות מת וגו' והימים הראשונים יפלו" — אם נטמא במת קודם הבאת קרבנותיו, סותר:
Rashi on Pesachim 80b:4:5.english: The nazirite - For it is written concerning him (Numbers 6): "And if [anyone] dies [very suddenly beside him]... and the prior days shall be void" — if he becomes ritually impure through a corpse before bringing his offerings, he forfeits [his previous days].

Rashi on Pesachim 80b:4:6.hebrew: הציץ מרצה על טומאת הדם - ותגלחתו כשירה, ומותר לשתות יין ולטמא למתים:
Rashi on Pesachim 80b:4:6.english: The frontplate appeases [God] for impurity of the blood - And [in the case of a nazirite,] his shaving is valid, and he is permitted to drink wine and to become ritually impure from the dead.

Rashi on Pesachim 80b:4:7.hebrew: ואין הציץ מרצה על טומאת הגוף - ואם נטמא בעת הבאת קרבנותיו, סותר את הכל:
Rashi on Pesachim 80b:4:7.english: And the frontplate does not appease for impurity of the body - And if [the nazirite] became ritually impure at the time of bringing his offerings, he forfeits all [his days of naziriteship].

Rashi on Pesachim 80b:5:1.hebrew: נטמא גופו - בטומאת התהום, בטומאת ספק, כדמפרש בגמרא. הרי זה מרצה, דהלכה למשה מסיני היא דהותרה טומאת התהום להם, כדאמר בגמרא. ובתוספתא מפרש לה הכי: כיצד? אמרו לו: קבר היה עמך בבית שנכנסת בו, תחת האבן שישבת עליה — ונודע לו עד שלא עשה פסחו, צריך לעשות פסח שני; משעשה, אין צריך לעשות פסח שני. וכן נזיר שהיה הולך להביא קרבנותיו, אמרו לו: מת היה עמך בבית שנכנסת בו, ונודע לו — בין עד שלא הביא קרבנותיו, בין משהביא קרבנותיו — צריך להביא קרבן טומאה. אבל אמרו לו: קבר התהום עמך בבית שנכנסת בו, תחת האבן שישבת עליה — ונודע לו עד שלא הביא קרבנותיו, צריך להביא קרבן טומאה. ומהו קרבן טומאה? אשם ושתי תורים, ומתחיל למנות נזירות אחרת. בתוספת' דזבחים:
Rashi on Pesachim 80b:5:1.english: His body became impure - with ritual impurity of the deep, [that is,] with uncertain ritual impurity, as [is] explained in the Gemara. [The frontplate] appeases [God], for it is a law [given] to Moses at Sinai that ritual impurity of the deep was permitted to them, as it says in the Gemara. And in the Tosefta it explains it thus: How so? [If] they said to him, "There was a grave with you in the house that you entered, under the stone upon which you sat" — [if] it became known to him before he offered his Paschal lamb, he must observe the second Pesach; [if] after he offered [it], he does not need to observe the second Pesach. And similarly, a Nazirite who was going to bring his offerings, [and] they said to him, "There was a corpse with you in the house that you entered," and it became known to him — whether before he brought his offerings or after he brought his offerings — he must bring an offering of ritual impurity. However, [if] they said to him, "A grave of the deep [was] with you in the house that you entered, under the stone upon which you sat" — [if] it became known to him before he brought his offerings, he must bring an offering of ritual impurity. And what is the offering of ritual impurity? A guilt-offering and two turtledoves, and he begins to count another [term of] Naziriteship. In Tosefta Zevachim.

Rashi on Pesachim 80b:7:1.hebrew: בין בשוגג בין במזיד - קס"ד דהכי קאמר שזרקו בין בשוגג בין במזיד, ומשני דהאי שוגג ומזיד אטומאה קאי, אבל זריקה בעינן שוגג:
Rashi on Pesachim 80b:7:1.english: Whether unwittingly or intentionally - [The Gemara] initially assumed that this is what it means: that [the priest] sprinkled [the blood] whether unwittingly or intentionally. And [the Gemara] answers that this "unwittingly or intentionally" refers to the [contracting of] impurity, whereas [for the] sprinkling we require [that it be done] unwittingly.

Tosafot on Pesachim 80b:11:1.hebrew: הוא הדין נודע ואחר כך נזרק - וא"ת, א"כ מאי דוחקיה דר' שילא לחלק בין טומאה לזריקתו, כיון דלאו דווקא קתני במתניתין "נזרק ואח"כ נודע"? ואומר ר"י, דר' שילא לאו אהך קושיא אמרה, אלא אמאי דפריך בהקומץ רבה (מנחות דף כה:) אהך ברייתא ד"על מה הציץ מרצה", מברייתא דקתני "דם שנטמא וזרקו, בשוגג — הורצה, במזיד — לא הורצה"; והכא אסיק ליה אגב תירוצא דרבינא:
Tosafot on Pesachim 80b:11:1.english: The same is true [if it] became known and was subsequently sprinkled - And if you ask: If so, what forced R' Shila to distinguish between [its] becoming impure and its sprinkling, since the Mishnah did not teach "it was sprinkled and subsequently became known" precisely? And R' Yitzchak says that R' Shila did not state it [in response] to this difficulty, rather [in response] to that which [the Gemara] asks in [chapter] HaKometz Rabbah (Menachot 25b) against this baraita of "For what does the frontplate appease," from a baraita that teaches: "Blood that became impure and one sprinkled it: [if] unwittingly, it is accepted; [if] intentionally, it is not accepted"; and here [the Gemara] cited it incidentally alongside Ravina's resolution.

Tosafot on Pesachim 80b:14:1.hebrew: לאו למעוטי טומאת התהום דשרץ - וא"ת: היכי שייך טומאת התהום בשרץ? והא לא מטמא אלא במגע, וטומאת התהום אינה בגלוי אלא מכוסה וטמון בעפר, בתבן או בצרור, כדתניא לקמן (פסחים דף פא:)? ויש לומר: כגון שהכניס ידו בעפר ונגע:
Tosafot on Pesachim 80b:14:1.english: "Is it not to exclude impurity of the deep of a creeping animal?" - And if you ask: How does impurity of the deep apply to a creeping animal? For it only imparts impurity through contact, whereas impurity of the deep is not exposed, but rather covered and hidden in earth, in straw, or in pebbles, as was taught in a baraita later (Pesachim 81b)? And one can answer: [It refers to] a case where he inserted his hand into the earth and touched [the creeping animal].

Tosafot on Pesachim 80b:15:1.hebrew: אי בנזיר וכי ימות מת עליו אמר רחמנא - תימה לר"י: דילמא לעולם בנזיר, ונפקא מינה אם שחט קרבנות ונטמא, דלא מרצי ציץ. וכן קשה בסמוך דקאמר: "אלא למ"ד שוחטין וזורקין כו'", הא מכל מקום נפקא מינה לאם שחט פסחו כדפי'? ואומר ר"י דלא בעי למימר הכי, דא"כ תיפשוט דבזיבחא גמירי, לא שנא בבעלים ול"ש בכהן:
Tosafot on Pesachim 80b:15:1.english: "If [it applies] to a nazirite, and 'When a man dies beside him' the Merciful One states" - This is astonishing to Ri: Perhaps [the baraita] is indeed dealing with a nazirite, and the practical difference is if he slaughtered [his] offerings and became impure [from a creeping animal], in which case the frontplate [of the High Priest] does not effect acceptance. And similarly, it is difficult [to understand what the Gemara says] shortly below, where it states: "Rather, according to the one who says one may slaughter and sprinkle [for those impure from a creeping animal], etc." — for in any event, there is a practical difference regarding if he slaughtered his Paschal lamb [and became impure], as I explained! And Ri says that [the Gemara] did not want to say this, because if so, you would resolve [the question and conclude] that [the leniency of impurity of the deep] was learned as a tradition regarding [the time of] slaughter, whether for the owners or for the priest.

Tosafot on Pesachim 80b:3:1.hebrew: בראשון לא עבדי הגדילו זבין על הטהורין כו' - נראה לר"י דס"ל כרב ולא כשמואל, דאמר "ויעשו את הפסח במועדו" מאי עבדת ביה, דלדידיה כיון שאין רוב טהורין — לא מידחו טמאים לפסח שני:
Tosafot on Pesachim 80b:3:1.english: On the first [Pesaḥ], they do not perform [the ritual]: the zavim outnumbered the ritually pure, etc. - It appears to R"I that [the Tanna] holds like Rav, and not like Shmuel, who said, "'And let them make the Paschal offering in its appointed time' — what do you do with it?" For according to him [Shmuel], since there is no majority of ritually pure [people], the ritually impure are not deferred to the second Pesaḥ.

Tosafot on Pesachim 80b:4:1.hebrew: נזרק דמו ואח"כ נודע שהוא טמא כו' - פי' בקונטרס שהוא טמא הדם או הבשר. וקשה לריב"א, דבטומאת בשר ע"כ ציץ לא מרצה לאכילה אלא לפטור מפסח שני, וכמ"ד הציץ מרצה על אכילות, וכר' נתן דלא בעי אלא גברא דחזי. וא"כ היכי דייק: טעמא דנזרק ואח"כ נודע, הא נודע ואח"כ נזרק לא מרצה ציץ — והיינו לפוטרו מפסח שני! וע"כ הא דלא מרצי היינו מדרבנן, מדמפליג בין שוגג למזיד, וכן אמר בהאשה רבה (יבמות דף צ. ושם); והיכי מחייבי ליה רבנן בפסח שני? כיון דמדאורייתא פטור, הוי חולין בעזרה! ועוד, הא לעיל (פסחים דף עח:) תנן: "נטמא בשר וחלב קיים, אינו זורק את הדם", והיינו מדרבנן דמוקי לה כרבי נתן; וא"כ הא דדייק רב לעיל: "אם זרק, הורצה" — היינו אפילו מדרבנן, ונודע קודם זריקה מיירי מדקאמר "לא יזרוק"! ונראה לריב"א דלא מיירי מתני' אלא בטומאת דם, והא דדייק בגמ': "הא נודע ואחר כך נזרק לא" — היינו להתיר בשר באכילה, אבל פטור מלעשות פסח שני. מיהו יש ליישב פירוש הקונטרס: דהא דקאמר "הציץ מרצה", היינו להקטיר האימורין; הא נודע ואח"כ נזרק, לא מרצה להקטיר האימורים, ופטור מפסח שני:
Tosafot on Pesachim 80b:4:1.english: "If its blood was sprinkled and afterwards it became known that it was impure, etc." - Rashi explained that [what became impure] was the blood or the meat. And Riva has a difficulty: regarding impurity of the meat, perforce the frontplate does not appease for eating [the meat], rather [it appeases] to exempt [the owners] from the second Pesaḥ — and [this is] according to the one who says that the frontplate appeases for [impurity affecting] consumption, and like Rabbi Natan who requires only a person who is fit [at the time of sprinkling]. If so, how does [the Gemara] infer: the reason [it appeases] is that it was sprinkled and afterwards it became known, implying that if it became known and afterwards it was sprinkled, the frontplate does not appease — which means [not appeasing] to exempt him from the second Pesaḥ! And perforce, that which it does not appease is [only] by rabbinic law, since [the Gemara] distinguishes between unwitting and intentional [transgression], and so [the Gemara] said in [the chapter] HaIshah Rabbah (Yevamot 90a and there); but how could the Rabbis obligate him in the second Pesaḥ? Since by Torah law he is exempt, it would be [bringing] non-sacred animals into the Temple courtyard! Furthermore, behold above (Pesaḥim 78b) we learned in a Mishnah: "If the meat became impure while the fat remains [pure], he may not sprinkle the blood" — and that is by rabbinic law, for [the Gemara] establishes it according to Rabbi Natan; if so, that which Rav inferred above: "If he sprinkled, it is appeased" — that is even by rabbinic law, and it is speaking of where it became known before sprinkling, since it states "he may not sprinkle"! Therefore, it appears to Riva that our Mishnah is speaking only of impurity of the blood, and that which the Gemara infers: "implying that if it became known and afterwards it was sprinkled, [it does] not [appease]" — that is to permit the meat for eating, but he is exempt from observing the second Pesaḥ. However, one can reconcile Rashi's explanation: that which [the Mishnah] says "the frontplate appeases" means to burn the sacrificial parts [on the altar]; implying that if it became known and afterwards it was sprinkled, it does not appease to burn the sacrificial parts, yet he is exempt from the second Pesaḥ.
